text:
maria: FYI enabling FP8 on the H100 cluster for the 13B inference pool is causing intermittent OOMs and occasional NaN logits in the v1.3 runtime profile :grimacing:

simon: can you paste the runtime config you used? transformer-engine flags, kernels selected, anything unusual? :eyes:

maria: sure. small snippet below — we flipped `enable_fp8=true` and used TE autopick:
```
transformer_engine:
  fp8_enabled: true
  fp8_autocast: true
  kernel_policy: AUTO
  max_seq: 2048
  kv_cache.shared: true
```
Logs show kernel picks: `te_fused attention_fp8_k1`, then fallback to `attn_sm80_fp16` before crash.

alex: hmmm autopick can choose unstable kernels for certain sequence layouts. Did you run the kernel-calibrator pass? We added a calibrate step to avoid FP8 underflows on L40S/H100 differences.

maria: yes ran calibrator with default sample set. Perf profile attached in thread (summary below) — latency went down 28% on tail p99 but error rate jumped ~0.6% (NaNs / inference failures).

lia: quick thought — are we running mixed batch sizes with cold KV cache starts? autopick sometimes picks an FP8 kernel optimized for long sequences but it behaves badly when KV cache is empty and we do many short chats. Kernel selection metric currently biases for peak throughput, not stability.

jordan: adding to that — batching heuristics: we fold across user session ids which causes variable seq distribution inside a batch. FP8 is sensitive to activation scale; mixed seqs -> more calibration misses. We should try conservative kernel policy for latency-sensitive channels, or use per-batch quant-scale recompute.

perf-bot: profile summary (1768001234-1768001500): avg tokens/sec H100 FP16=5200, FP8=6800, p99 latency FP16=210ms, FP8=150ms, NaN-failure-rate FP16=0.02%, FP8=0.64%.

alex: thanks perf-bot. Those throughput wins look real but stability regressions are nontrivial. Suggest: 1) run kernel warmup on each worker with synthetic KV-sequence patterns 2) disable FP8 kernel policy for short-seq workloads 3) instrument per-kernel NaN counters.

maria: tried warmup — reduced NaN rate by ~40% but some crashes persisted. Also saw that TE config `fp8_autocast=true` sometimes leaves residual scale state between requests when we use shared KV cache across GPUs. Could be a bug in KV state reset after context switch.

lia: good catch. KV cache shared=true is suspicious. Do we have a deterministic barrier between sessions? If FP8 scale params are stored per-GPU but reused across user contexts, they can corrupt next request.

simon: can you repro with `kv_cache.shared=false`? If that removes the issue it's a strong signal. Also try `kernel_policy=STABLE` (our policy that avoids experimental fused kernels).

maria: repro matrix attached. With `kv_cache.shared=false` + `kernel_policy=STABLE` no NaNs in ~12k requests, but p50 latency regresses ~10% compared to FP8 autopick. So trade-off between latency and correctness.

jordan: we should add a runtime guard: if NaN rate per-worker > 0.1% over a minute, auto-fallback to STABLE policy and flush FP8 per-kernel scale state. That buys safety while keeping FP8 for healthy workers.

alex: agreed. Also propose a lightweight calibrator during startup that runs 3 micro-batches with representative seq lengths and records scale ranges; use that to seed the FP8 kernel parameters. This is cheaper than full dataset calibration and might prevent the first-request NaNs.

lia: for L40S differences — its TensorCore fp8 primitives have slightly different dynamic range; we need per-GPU model profiles. Add a label in kernel catalog for `fp8_range_profile: L40S_v2` vs `H100_v3` and restrict autopick to compatible profiles.

perf-bot: added ticket PERF-7321 to track: "FP8 stability: KV cache isolation, kernel warmup, per-gpu fp8 profiles, autoswitch policy". Estimated priority: high.

deploy-bot: rolling canary of new guard/auto-fallback pushed to h100-canary-2 at 1768001300. Monitor p99 and NaN counters.

maria: can folks help monitor the canary for the next 2 hours? I'll collect kernel-level traces. Also I'll run a synthetic short-seq heavy workload against L40S to see if profile mismatch shows up.

simon: I'll set up dashboard alerts on `worker.fp8.nan_rate` and `worker.kernel_policy_fallbacks`. alex and jordan can assist with adding warmup + per-batch scale recompute PRs.

alex: starting the warmup PR — small change, adds 3-step calibrate on worker init, opt-out via `fp8_warmup=false`.

jordan: I'll prototype the auto-fallback loop and the state flush. Expect a draft by EOD.

maria: thanks all. If anyone has L40S hardware access, ping me — I'd like to compare per-kernel perf counters. Also saved traces under gs://redwood-perf/fp8/1768001234/trace.pb.

lia: one more note — add a test to the perf-suite that replays mixed-batch seq distributions; caught these before in int8 work.

maria: yep will add. Thanks :thumbsup:
